turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Doctor, I am really worried, so kindly bear with my questions. My right knee has been paining for about five months, worst when I go down the stairs, and at night it wakes me up.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Swelling, locking, or giving way?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): No swelling. It does not lock, and it has not given way. I am only scared because the pain is there at night.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Inner side or outer?

[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Inner side. Coming up the stairs is manageable, going down is bad, and at night it throbs. Is night pain a dangerous thing, doctor? I was awake at two o'clock thinking the worst.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Common in wear and tear. Not dangerous by itself. Are you on a gel or tablets?

[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): Diclofenac gel, the one percent, morning and night. If the night is very bad I put a third layer, even though the chemist said twice is enough. I hope that is not harmful.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tablets too?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): Sometimes, from the pharmacy only. Diclofenac fifty milligram by mouth, two or three times in a week, when the pain is too much.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any stomach trouble with those?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): No. No stomach problem at all.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): No swelling on the knee. Tender along the inner joint line. The bend stops short of full, and it straightens fully.
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): Is a short bend serious? Will this end in an operation? My neighbour had a replacement, the whole story was frightening, and, um, sorry, that is not your question.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): No operation talk today. How is the weight?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): I have stopped my morning walk because of the knee. Last time they said eighty eight kilos, and I feel I am heavier now. Is the weight damaging the joint?
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Scale says eighty six point five kilograms. BP is one forty two over eighty eight. Pulse is seventy six.
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): Eighty six point five, not eighty eight, alright. Still, how many kilos should I lose, five or ten? If you don't give a number I will worry all week.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): No target today. Smaller portions, less rice, a few kilos, slowly.
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): Are fruits allowed? My brother had a stroke, so weight and BP make me very anxious. Is one forty two very high?
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mildly raised, not an emergency. Fruits are fine. Any sugar disease?

[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): Last year they did a fasting sugar, and they said it was borderline. I don't remember any number, only that it was borderline and not diabetes. I take no tablets for sugar.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright. Is the stomach still fine with the diclofenac?

[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): Well, actually, I need to correct that. I do get heartburn, a burning in the chest after that tablet, for a few weeks, and I cannot say which day it started. Last week I thought it was my heart. Do I need a scope, is it an ulcer?
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Stop the diclofenac tablets. Continue the gel twice a day, a thin layer, not three times. No scope today.
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): Even if the night pain is bad, stop fully? Gel alone was not enough, I have already tried that. Then what do I take, doctor, please?
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Paracetamol, one gram by mouth, up to three times a day when it hurts. That is two tablets of five hundred milligrams. Do not take it with the diclofenac tablet.
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): Is that safe with the borderline sugar, and are there side effects? I have no allergies.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): It is safe with the sugar. No drug allergy, confirm?
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): No drug allergy. None at all.
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): For the burning, may I take pantoprazole? My wife takes twenty milligram, but that strip is hers, not mine. I should not use someone else's tablet, no?
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do not take hers. No pantoprazole for you today. The burning should ease once you stop the tablet, and if it carries on we look at it again.

[SEG0032] person_1 (PATIENT): If it carries on, do you mean I come back, or a camera test? What about physiotherapy versus the injection? My daughter sent a steroid injection video about cartilage damage, and I hardly slept. Which one are you choosing?
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not choosing today. Physiotherapy, or a knee injection if the pain is still limiting you. Both are only options, and we decide next visit.
[SEG0034] person_1 (PATIENT): So physio is not booked now? If I get worse in between, what should I do? How many weeks until I see you?
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come back in six weeks. If the pain shoots up, or the knee locks, come earlier.

[SEG0036] person_1 (PATIENT): Six weeks, okay. I stay on the second floor and there is no lift, so the stairs are daily. Should I avoid stairs completely? I already go down sideways, like a very old man, which makes me sad.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do not avoid the stairs. Go slowly and hold the rail. Avoiding them will weaken the knee.
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): Slowly, with the rail, understood. I will keep the gel to twice, not the third time. I was overdoing it from fear, sorry.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Twice. Thin layer. That is enough.

[SEG0040] person_1 (PATIENT): Let me repeat so I don't mix it up. Paracetamol one gram, two of the five hundreds, up to three times, and no diclofenac tablet from the chemist. The gel is one percent, twice a day. May I use the gel and the paracetamol on the same day?
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, same day is fine. A night dose is fine too, as long as it is not a fourth.

[SEG0042] person_1 (PATIENT): Is it osteoarthritis, tell me straight. I keep fearing a tumour, and some nights the worry itself keeps me awake more than the pain. I am not sleeping properly because of that anxiety.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): This fits osteoarthritis, wear and tear of the knee. It is not a tumour. No scan today.
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): I am sixty eight, is that early? My uncle had both knees replaced when he was seventy. Does this kind of thing run in the family, should I be more worried?
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sixty eight is a usual age for it. Your uncle's operations do not decide your knee.
[SEG0046] person_1 (PATIENT): And the borderline sugar, can we repeat that test? They said borderline and nobody called me back. I am frightened it has become diabetes without my knowing.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not at this visit. Mention it to your regular doctor. Today we are sorting the knee.

[SEG0048] person_1 (PATIENT): I will mention it. On the heartburn, I truly cannot date the start, a few weeks is all I can say. I briefly thought it was there before the tablets, but no, it comes after the tablets. Sorry, I go back and forth when I am nervous.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): After the tablets, then. Stopping them is the treatment for that burning. We have covered it.

[SEG0050] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, I have it, I think. Gel and paracetamol same day, six weeks, sooner if the pain shoots up or the knee locks, and physio or injection not decided yet. Did I leave out any question? I always feel I have.
[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): You have the plan. Reception will book the six weeks.
[SEG0052] person_1 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. I will try not to search knee pain on the phone tonight, because last time I did that I did not sleep at all.
[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): Don't search tonight. Take what I prescribed, and come as arranged.
